reason: The contract (problem.txt) requires every output element to equal the sequential affine recurrence exactly with abs/rel tolerance 0 for all legal inputs (1<=N<=32, 1<=B<=64, all legal int8/int16 values). Two independent runtime probes on the frozen Triton 3.4.0/T4 environment show run() != reference(): probe t10 (claim c1) found 16/64 mismatching cases at N=25 (chunks=4), with first bad step 24 — the last step of the last chunk, consistent with an incorrect exclusive inter-chunk carry produced by the hand-rolled _exclusive_chunks up/down tree in _block_carries; probe t15 (claim c3) ran a 162-case full-domain sweep (every N in 1..32 with B in {1,64}, extreme int16 values, singular/all-zero matrices, nonzero-storage-offset contiguous views) and found 27 mismatches at N=25..32 for both B=1 and B=64. All failing inputs are legal and squarely in the declared domain, so this is a confirmed in-scope correctness failure of a contract-required exact-equality invariant, not a tolerance, representation, or generalization artifact. Claim c2 (local 6-tuple associative_scan) was rebutted by a clean 40/40 N<=8 sweep and does not mitigate the defect. The exclusive-carry defect confirmed by c1/c3 is not accounted for by any contract clause.
